column1: =每天一點，日積月累。這是一個陪你專注、推進長期計畫、照顧身心的練習空間。接下來用幾張卡片，帶你認識最重要的用法。
column2: A little every day adds up. This is a space to help you focus, move long projects forward and look after yourself. The next few cards show you the most important parts.

column1: =寫下今天最重要的三件事，按下番茄鐘開始專注。暫停時可以記下停在哪裡；冒出雜念就丟進「雜念停車場」。每段結束花十秒記下做了什麼，月曆和統計會自動累積。
column2: Write down today’s three most important things and start the Pomodoro timer. When you pause, note where you stopped; when a stray thought pops up, drop it in the “Distraction parking lot”. After each session, take ten seconds to log what you did — the calendar and stats add it up for you.

column2: “My rhythm” is a 12-minute questionnaire that finds your daily energy peak and dip and what motivates you most, then suggests a plan for your day. You can do it in parts — each part shows you its results right away.

column2: Plan practice by question type: which type today, which problem to solve, and how. Bring one type’s error rate down before moving to the next — you’ll feel progress every day. If a method doesn’t work, try another or talk it through with a teacher or classmates. Also check that your ID is still valid.

column2: Work through every question type once and find your problems: which type do you miss most, and why? Which takes the most time? No need for full mock exams yet — that’s for the last week.

column1: =列出未完成的項目，最模糊的先動一點，需要幫忙的早點開口。

column2: List what’s left and put it in order.

column2: When you’re stuck, ask a teacher or classmate.

column1: =固定作息，讓身體習慣考試的時段。
column2: Keep a fixed routine so your body gets used to the exam time.

column1: =好好休息，之後再回頭記下心得。
column2: Rest well, then come back and note what you learned.
Focus on the one thing that matters most.

column2: Bring your ID, eat something, breathe. Just show what you know.

column1: =帶齊證件，帶件外套。吃早餐、活動一下筋骨，先唸幾句幫自己暖身。考試只是把累積的展現出來，不是評斷你這個人。可以不完美，但不要輕易放棄。考完先好好吃一頓，再把題目回憶和表現記下來，之後檢討很有用。
column2: Bring your ID and a jacket. Eat breakfast, stretch, and say a few lines out loud to warm up. The exam just shows what you’ve built — it doesn’t judge who you are. It’s fine not to be perfect, but don’t give up easily. Afterwards, have a good meal, then note what you remember and how you did — it helps a lot when you review.

column1: =靜心回饋與雁書加入聖嚴法師《牛的印跡》（Hoofprint of the Ox）：昏沉時的跪姿、念頭像牧牛、練習像調琴弦、十牛圖等
column2: Meditation feedback and Yanshu letters now draw on Master Sheng Yen’s Hoofprint of the Ox: a kneeling posture for drowsiness, herding thoughts like an ox, tuning practice like a harp string, the Ten Oxherding Pictures and more

column1: =靜心回饋：先挑最貼近你這次寫下內容的說明，老師輪流退到第二；另一本書也說到同一點時，附在「也可以這樣看」；同樣的困難最近反覆出現，會換個角度說，並溫和地多問一句
column2: Meditation feedback: the explanation closest to what you wrote comes first, with teacher rotation second; when another book makes the same point, it appears under “Another way to see it”; when the same difficulty keeps coming back, the feedback takes a new angle and gently asks a question

column1: =靜心回饋加入智者大師《修習止觀坐禪法要》（小止觀）：調身調息調心、不沈不浮、五蓋、出定的順序等，可以指定由智者大師回應
column2: Meditation feedback now includes Master Zhiyi’s Essentials of Practising Calm and Insight (the “Lesser Calm and Insight”): adjusting body, breath and mind, neither sinking nor floating, the five hindrances, how to come out of sitting — and you can choose Zhiyi as your teacher

column1: =隔年飯插上春花，叫「萬年糧」，祈願年年有餘。今晚放下工作，好好和家人吃頓飯。
column2: Last year’s rice topped with spring flowers — “grain for ten thousand years”, a wish for plenty. Tonight, set work aside and share a good meal with family.

column1: =門上貼福，迎接新歲。寫下今年想慢慢培養的一個習慣，每天做一點就好。
column2: A “fu” on the door welcomes the new year. Write down one habit you’d like to grow slowly this year — a little each day.

column1: =提燈、賞燈、猜燈謎，年節在燈火裡收尾。把這個月最想完成的一件事，當成一盞燈掛在心上。
column2: Lanterns, lantern riddles — the New Year ends in lamplight. Hang the one thing you most want to finish this month in your mind like a lantern.

column1: =包粽子、掛艾草、划龍舟。正午陽氣最盛，最需要力氣的事放在上午，午後多喝水。
column2: Rice dumplings, mugwort, dragon boats. Noon is at its strongest — do the hardest things in the morning and drink plenty in the afternoon.

column1: =供月餅、擺果盤，等月亮升起，一家團圓。今晚放下手機，靜靜看一會兒月亮。
column2: Mooncakes and fruit laid out, waiting for the moon with family. Tonight, put your phone down and watch the moon for a while.

column1: =一元復始，萬象更新。替新的一年寫一張新禧帖：一件想慢慢做的事就好。
column2: Everything begins anew. Write a New Year card to the year ahead — just one thing you’d like to do slowly.

column1: =國定假日，放假一天。放慢腳步，想想珍惜的人與事。
column2: A national holiday — a day off. Slow down and think of the people and things you cherish.

column1: =放一隻風箏，讓童心飛高一點。找一件小時候喜歡的事做做看。
column2: Fly a kite and let your inner child soar. Try something you loved as a kid.

column1: =國定假日，放假一天。辛苦了，今天把休息也排進行程。
column2: A national holiday — a day off. You’ve worked hard; put rest on today’s schedule too.

column1: =「上大人，孔乙己」，舊時學童的第一張描紅。想起一位影響過你的老師，寫一句謝謝。
column2: “Shang da ren, Kong Yi Ji” — the first tracing sheet of children long ago. Think of a teacher who shaped you and write a line of thanks.

column1: =國定假日，放假一天。留一段時間給自己，也留一段給家人朋友。
column2: A national holiday — a day off. Keep some time for yourself, and some for family and friends.

column1: =國定假日，放假一天。留一點空白給自己，散步、看看天空。
column2: A national holiday — a day off. Leave some blank space for yourself: a walk, a look at the sky.

column1: =國定假日，放假一天。一年快到尾聲，寫下今年最想感謝的三件事。
column2: A national holiday — a day off. The year is nearly over; write down three things you’re most grateful for.

column1: =「我的頁面」裡的每日打卡，在今日就能打卡
column2: Check off the daily habits from your pages right on Today

column1: =還沒有每日打卡。到「＋ 新增頁面」選「習慣養成」，或在任何頁面加一個「每日打卡」區塊。
column2: No daily habits yet. Use “+ New page” and choose “Habit building”, or add a “Daily check-in” block to any page.

column1: =前一晚把明天要讀的書翻到那一頁、放在桌上；專注時把手機放到另一個房間。想做的事看得見，會分心的東西拿不到，開始就容易得多。
column2: The night before, open tomorrow’s book to the right page and leave it on your desk; while focusing, put your phone in another room. When what you want to do is in sight and distractions are out of reach, starting gets much easier.

column1: =「刷完牙之後，我會讀一頁書」比「我要多讀書」更容易做到。也可以設一個兩分鐘版本，累的時候做它就算數。
column2: “After I brush my teeth, I’ll read one page” is easier to keep than “I’ll read more”. You can also set a two-minute version — on tired days, doing that counts.

column1: =趁休息，把下一顆番茄要用的東西擺到手邊。
column2: Use the break to put what you need for the next Pomodoro within reach.

column1: =開始下一顆前，把手機放遠一點。
column2: Before the next Pomodoro, move your phone a little farther away.

column1: =桌上只留下一件要做的事，其他的先收起來。
column2: Leave only the one task on your desk; put the rest away for now.
Keep your water glass where you can see it.

column1: =寫下什麼時候、在哪裡做，或接在哪件事之後，比只說「我要做」更容易做到。
column2: Writing down when and where you’ll do it — or what it follows — makes it easier than just saying “I will”.
e.g. every morning at 7:30, at my desk

column1: =接在哪件事之後（選填，比時間更好記）
column2: After what (optional — easier to remember than a time)
e.g. after pouring coffee, after brushing my teeth

column1: =兩分鐘版本（累的時候做這個就算數）
column2: Two-minute version (on tired days, this counts)

column1: =例：讀一頁、穿上跑鞋、坐下來一分鐘
column2: e.g. read one page, put on running shoes, sit for one minute

column1: =例：持續閱讀的人、照顧身體的人
column2: e.g. someone who keeps reading, someone who looks after their body
How you’ll set up your space (optional)

column1: =讓想做的事看得見、容易開始；讓會分心的東西不方便拿到。每打一次卡，就是為想成為的自己投一票。
column2: Make what you want to do visible and easy to start; make distractions hard to reach. Every check-in is a vote for the person you want to become.

column1: =做了最小版，也算數。習慣靠的是不中斷，不是每次都做滿。
column2: You did the mini version — it counts. Habits grow from not breaking, not from doing it all every time.

column1: =今天用兩分鐘版本接上了，這比完美更重要。
column2: You kept it going today with the two-minute version — that matters more than perfect.

column1: =小小的一步也是一票，明天有力氣再做多一點。
column2: A small step is still a vote. Do a bit more tomorrow if you have the energy.
Done for today — pick it up again tomorrow.

column1: =做到了。明天同一個時間，再來一次。
column2: Done. Same time tomorrow, once more.

column1: =昨天休息了，今天接回來就好，休一天不算中斷。
column2: You rested yesterday — just pick it up today. One day off doesn’t break the chain.
days · one day off doesn’t break it

column1: =記下了，今天的這一票投下了
=每日打卡升級：寫一句「什麼時候、在哪裡做」或「接在哪件事之後」；設一個兩分鐘版本，累的時候做它也算數；休一天不算中斷，別連續錯過兩天就好；寫下想成為的人，每次打卡就是投一票。今日頁可以加「習慣打卡」小卡
column2: Daily check-in upgrade: write when and where (or after what) you’ll do it; set a two-minute version that counts on tired days; one day off doesn’t break the chain — just don’t miss twice; name who you want to be, and each check-in is a vote. Add the “Habit check-in” card to Today

column1: =環境設計的小提示：讓想做的事看得見、會分心的東西拿不到（提示卡、番茄鐘休息時、習慣設定）
column2: Environment tips: keep what you want to do in sight and distractions out of reach (tip cards, Pomodoro breaks, habit setup)

column1: =節日小卡：元旦、除夕、春節、元宵、兒童節、端午、教師節、中秋配上《清俗紀聞》（1799）的木刻插圖；春節卡從初一顯示到初三；光復節、行憲紀念日更新
column2: Holiday cards: New Year’s Day, Lunar New Year’s Eve, Lunar New Year, Lantern Festival, Children’s Day, Dragon Boat, Teachers’ Day and Mid-Autumn now carry woodblock illustrations from Qingsu Jiwen (1799); the Lunar New Year card shows from day 1 to day 3; Retrocession Day and Constitution Day updated

column1: =靜心回饋與雁書的說法不再每次一樣；兩本書的觀點自然接在一起；反覆遇到同樣困難時，不會每次都追問
column2: Meditation feedback and Yanshu replies vary their wording; views from two books flow together naturally; recurring difficulties don’t get a follow-up question every time

column1: =昨天休息了，今天一顆番茄接回來就好，休一天不算中斷。
column2: You rested yesterday — one Pomodoro today picks it back up. One day off doesn’t break the chain.

column1: =昨天停了一天很正常。別連續錯過兩天，今天做一點就接上了。
column2: Taking yesterday off is normal. Just don’t miss two in a row — a little today keeps it going.

column1: =休息過了，今天從一件小事開始，節奏就回來了。
column2: You’ve had your rest. Start with one small thing today and the rhythm comes back.

column1: =好幾天沒開始了，沒關係。今天只要坐下來兩分鐘，剩下的交給開始之後。
column2: It’s been a few days — that’s okay. Just sit down for two minutes today; let the rest follow once you’ve started.

column1: =寫上什麼時候做，例如「10:00 回覆報價」「午飯後 讀 10 頁」，會比只寫事情更容易做到。
column2: Add when you’ll do it — “10:00 send the quote”, “after lunch read 10 pages” — it’s easier to follow through than a bare task.

column1: =明天打開日課，這三件會直接出現在「今天最重要的三件事」。睡前把第一件事要用的東西擺好，明天一坐下就能開始。
column2: When you open Rike tomorrow, these three will be your “three most important things today”. Before bed, set out what the first one needs so you can start the moment you sit down.

column1: =中間休一天不算中斷，連續兩天沒做才重新算
column2: One day off doesn’t break it; it restarts after two days in a row

column1: =好習慣設計用在整個 App：連續天數改成休一天不算中斷（統計、靜心、計畫）；今日頁在休息一天後提醒接回來，隔好幾天就從兩分鐘開始；三件事建議寫上什麼時候做；睡前把明天要用的東西擺好；提示卡與番茄鐘休息時加入環境安排的小提示
column2: Good-habit design across the app: streaks now survive a single day off (stats, meditation, plans); Today nudges you to pick things back up after a day off, and suggests starting with two minutes after a longer gap; add a time to your three things; set out tomorrow’s things before bed; tip cards and Pomodoro breaks include small environment tips

column1: =遇到問題，我想先自己想辦法，而不是馬上照別人的做法。
column2: When a problem comes up, I want to work it out myself before following someone else’s way.

column1: =能自己安排時間和進度，我會做得更好。
column2: I do better when I can set my own schedule and pace.

column1: =我喜歡發展自己的看法，即使和大家不同。
column2: I like forming my own views, even when they differ from everyone else’s.

column1: =如果只能照指示做事，我會很快失去興趣。
column2: If I can only follow instructions, I lose interest quickly.

column1: =我會主動找新的地方、新的活動或新的人。
column2: I go looking for new places, new activities or new people.

column1: =比起穩定，我更想要有變化、有點冒險的生活。
column2: I’d rather have a life with change and a bit of adventure than one that’s stable.

column1: =學一樣全新的東西，會讓我很興奮。
column2: Learning something completely new excites me.

column1: =同樣的事做太久，我會想換個方式或換個挑戰。
column2: If I do the same thing too long, I want a new approach or a new challenge.

column1: =吃一頓好吃的、睡個好覺，對我來說很有價值。
column2: A good meal and a good night’s sleep matter a lot to me.

column1: =我會特地安排時間，做讓自己開心的事。
column2: I make a point of setting aside time for things that make me happy.

column1: =我覺得人生應該好好享受，不必一直苦撐。
column2: I think life is for enjoying, not just for pushing through.

column1: =工作或讀書告一段落，我一定會好好犒賞自己。
column2: When I finish a stretch of work or study, I always treat myself.

column1: =我會替自己設定高標準，並努力達到。
column2: I set high standards for myself and work to meet them.

column1: =被肯定做得好，會讓我更有動力。
column2: Being recognised for doing well makes me more motivated.

column1: =我喜歡看看自己比以前進步了多少。
column2: I like seeing how much I’ve improved.

column1: =完成一個困難的目標，是我最有成就感的時候。
column2: Reaching a difficult goal is when I feel most accomplished.

column1: =我喜歡當負責人，帶著大家往前走。
column2: I like being the one in charge, leading everyone forward.

column1: =擁有足夠的資源或財力，讓我覺得比較有力量。
column2: Having enough resources or money makes me feel more powerful.

column1: =我希望別人照我的想法去做。
column2: I want others to do things my way.

column1: =有決定權的位置，對我很有吸引力。
column2: Positions where I get to decide appeal to me.

column1: =我會避免做可能讓自己難堪的事。
column2: I avoid doing things that might embarrass me.

column1: =別人怎麼看我，會影響我做決定。
column2: How others see me affects my decisions.

column1: =在大家面前，我希望表現得體、不出錯。
column2: In front of others, I want to appear proper and not make mistakes.

column1: =被當眾指出錯誤，會讓我很久都放不下。
column2: Being corrected in public stays with me for a long time.

column1: =先存好一筆錢或準備好備案，我才安心。
column2: I only feel at ease once I have savings or a backup plan.

column1: =我希望生活的環境安全、有秩序。
column2: I want my surroundings to be safe and orderly.

column1: =比起冒險的機會，我更喜歡穩定的選擇。
column2: I prefer a stable choice to a risky opportunity.

column1: =健康和家人的平安，是我最先考慮的事。
column2: Health and my family’s safety are the first things I consider.

column1: =我覺得延續家族或文化的傳統很重要。
column2: Carrying on family or cultural traditions is important to me.

column1: =有些事，我會照著長輩傳下來的方式做。
column2: For some things, I follow the ways passed down by my elders.

column1: =宗教或文化的信念，是我生活的一部分。
column2: Religious or cultural beliefs are part of my life.

column1: =我不太喜歡隨意改變大家習慣的做法。
column2: I don’t like changing established ways of doing things without reason.

column1: =即使不完全同意，我通常還是會照規定做。
column2: Even when I don’t fully agree, I usually follow the rules.

column1: =對長輩、老師或主管有禮貌，對我來說很重要。
column2: Being polite to elders, teachers or managers matters to me.

column1: =我會避免說出可能讓人不高興的話。
column2: I avoid saying things that might upset people.

column1: =答應別人的事，我一定會做到。
column2: When I promise something, I always follow through.

column1: =我不需要被特別注意，平凡就很好。
column2: I don’t need special attention; being ordinary is fine.

column1: =我覺得自己的成就，有很多是靠別人和運氣幫忙。
column2: I feel much of what I’ve achieved came from others and luck.

column1: =我不喜歡炫耀，也不想比別人特別。
column2: I don’t like showing off or standing out from others.

column1: =面對大自然或很大的事物，我覺得自己很渺小，也很踏實。
column2: Facing nature or something vast, I feel small — and grounded.

column1: =我希望每個人都被公平對待，即使是我不認識的人。
column2: I want everyone treated fairly, even people I don’t know.

column1: =我願意為了保護環境改變生活習慣。
column2: I’m willing to change my habits to protect the environment.

column1: =我會試著理解和我想法很不一樣的人。
column2: I try to understand people whose views are very different from mine.

column1: =世界上其他地方的苦難，也會讓我放在心上。
column2: Suffering in other parts of the world stays on my mind too.

column1: =我很在意身邊的人過得好不好。
column2: I care a lot about how the people around me are doing.

column1: =朋友有困難時，我願意花時間陪他。
column2: When a friend is struggling, I’m willing to spend time with them.

column1: =我希望自己是家人和朋友可以依靠的人。
column2: I want to be someone my family and friends can rely on.

column1: =能幫上身邊的人，讓我覺得很有意義。
column2: Being able to help those around me feels meaningful.

column1: =年前最後的忙碌，把該收尾的事收一收，留點力氣給明天的團圓。
column2: The last rush before the New Year — wrap up what needs wrapping up and save some energy for tomorrow’s reunion.

column1: =表格每天依最新紀錄重算；到了時間、紀錄也夠，跟「我的節奏」有明顯不同時，會先問你要不要更新。
column2: The table is recalculated daily from your latest records; when it’s time, there’s enough data and it clearly differs from My Rhythm, you’ll be asked before anything updates.

column1: =春節卡：前兩天是小年夜、前一天是除夕，春節從初一顯示到初五
column2: Lunar New Year card: two days before is Little New Year’s Eve, the day before is New Year’s Eve, and the card shows from day 1 to day 5

column1: =我的節奏：驅動力測驗的題庫變成三倍，每個價值都測兩句，「重新測驗」會換一批題目；作息的變化下方顯示下一次兩週比對與兩個月報告的時間
column2: My Rhythm: the drive quiz bank is three times larger — each value is still tested with two statements, and “Retake” draws a new set; the routine table now shows when the next two-week check and two-month report are due
Today’s note is at most three sentences

column1: =照你自己的步調來，今天想先推進哪一件，就從那件開始。
column2: Go at your own pace — whatever you most want to move forward today, start there.

column1: =今天試一個沒用過的做法，哪怕只是換張桌子坐。
column2: Try one new approach today, even if it’s just sitting at a different table.

column1: =先替自己準備一杯喜歡的飲料，舒服的開始會走得更遠。
column2: Make yourself a drink you like first — a comfortable start goes further.

column1: =替今天定一個看得見的小目標，做完就打個勾。
column2: Set one visible small goal for today and tick it off when it’s done.

column1: =先決定今天由你拍板的那件事，其他的再排。
column2: First decide the one thing you’ll call the shots on today, then arrange the rest.

column1: =先在沒人看的地方做個草稿，熟了再拿出來。
column2: Start with a draft nobody sees, and bring it out once it’s ready.

column1: =先把今天確定要做的事寫下來，心會比較安定。
column2: Write down what you’re sure to do today — your mind will settle.

column1: =照著平常的順序開始，熟悉的節奏會帶著你走。
column2: Start in your usual order; the familiar rhythm will carry you.

column1: =把答應過的事排在前面，做到了，心裡就踏實。
column2: Put your promises first — keeping them brings peace of mind.

column1: =不必和誰比，把手上這一件做好就好。
column2: No need to compare yourself; just do this one thing well.

column1: =想想這件事做好了，能讓誰過得好一點。
column2: Think about who this will help once it’s done well.

column1: =今天做的事，也是為了在乎的人，這份心意會撐著你。
column2: What you do today is also for the people you care about — that will hold you up.

column1: =今天哪個決定是你自己做的？那份自主，明天也帶著。
column2: Which decision today was truly yours? Carry that independence into tomorrow.

column1: =今天有什麼小小的新鮮事？記下來，明天再找一個。
column2: What small new thing happened today? Note it, and find another tomorrow.

column1: =今晚留一段時間給讓你開心的事，這也是充電。
column2: Keep some time tonight for something that makes you happy — that’s recharging too.

column1: =今天的進度記下來了嗎？一點一點，都算數。
column2: Did you log today’s progress? Every little bit counts.

column1: =今天你帶動了哪件事？明天想先掌握哪一件？
column2: What did you drive forward today? What do you want to take charge of first tomorrow?

column1: =今天做得不夠好的地方，就當成私下的練習吧。
column2: Whatever didn’t go well today, treat it as private practice.

column1: =今天完成的事，都是明天的底氣。
column2: What you finished today is tomorrow’s confidence.

column1: =今天的節奏穩嗎？穩下來，就是很好的一天。
column2: Was today’s rhythm steady? A steady day is a good day.

column1: =今天守住了哪個約定？給自己一點肯定。
column2: Which promise did you keep today? Give yourself some credit.

column1: =平凡地過完一天，也是一種踏實。
column2: An ordinary day, well lived, is its own kind of solid ground.

column1: =今天有沒有一個瞬間，你為別人想了一下？
column2: Was there a moment today when you thought of someone else?

column1: =今天有誰因為你而輕鬆一點？也謝謝願意付出的自己。
column2: Who had it a little easier today because of you? Thank yourself for giving, too.

column1: =今日小語：驅動力的話每天換說法；起床後、午後、傍晚、睡前這幾個時間點先說作息提醒，其他時候以驅動力的話為主
column2: Today’s note: drive lines vary from day to day; after waking, in the afternoon, early evening and before bed, the routine reminder comes first — at other times, the drive line leads

column1: =慢慢來，今天能往前一點點就好。
column2: Take it slowly — a little progress today is enough.

column1: =不必等到準備好，開始了就會越來越順。
column2: No need to wait until you’re ready; it gets easier once you start.

column1: =做不完的事，留一點給明天也沒關係。
column2: It’s fine to leave some of it for tomorrow.
You’re working harder than you think.

column1: =專心做好眼前這一件，就是今天最好的安排。
column2: Doing this one thing well is the best plan for today.

column1: =累了就停一下，休息也是前進的一部分。
column2: When you’re tired, pause — rest is part of moving forward.

column1: =今天也謝謝願意坐下來的自己。
column2: Thank yourself for sitting down today.

column1: =不用每件事都做到滿分，做完比做好更重要。
column2: Not everything needs full marks; done beats perfect.

column1: =忙的時候，三次慢慢的呼吸，也是一次小小的靜心。
column2: When you’re busy, three slow breaths are a small meditation too.

column1: =心浮起來時，先感覺腳底踩著地面，再回到手上的事。
column2: When your mind drifts up, feel your feet on the floor, then return to the task.

column1: =今天也可以留三分鐘，安靜地陪自己坐一下。
column2: You could keep three minutes today to sit quietly with yourself.

column1: =把注意力放回此刻正在做的這一件，心會慢慢定下來。
column2: Bring your attention back to what you’re doing now, and your mind will settle.

column1: =念頭跑掉了就溫和地帶回來，做事的時候也一樣。
column2: When your thoughts wander, gently bring them back — while working, too.

column1: =肩膀鬆一點、吐氣長一點，再繼續。
column2: Drop your shoulders, lengthen your out-breath, then carry on.

column1: =擔心的事，先寫下來交給紙，現在只做眼前能做的一件。
column2: Write your worries down and hand them to the page; for now, do the one thing you can.

column1: =不安的時候，呼吸放慢一點，事情一件一件來。
column2: When you feel uneasy, slow your breathing and take things one at a time.

column1: =今天只做兩分鐘的版本也算數，開始了就好。
column2: Even the two-minute version counts today — starting is what matters.

column1: =卡住的時候，把事情縮到最小，先做一小步。
column2: When you’re stuck, shrink it down and take one small step.

column1: =讀不進去時，起來走五分鐘再回來，大腦會在背後整理。
column2: When nothing sinks in, walk for five minutes; your brain keeps sorting in the background.

column1: =今天記不住的，隔幾天再複習，反而記得更牢。
column2: What won’t stick today will stick better if you review it again in a few days.

column1: =事情很多時，一次只放一件在心上，做完再換下一件。
column2: When there’s a lot, hold just one thing in mind; finish it, then move on.

column1: =下班前寫下明天的三件事，讓腦袋也能下班。
column2: Before you leave work, write tomorrow’s three things so your mind can clock off too.

column1: =想說的話，先用一句寫下結論，開口會比較清楚。
column2: Write your point in one sentence first; it’ll be clearer when you speak.

column1: =被誤解的感覺很難受，先照顧好自己的心情，再想怎麼說。
column2: Being misunderstood hurts; look after your feelings first, then think about what to say.

column1: =提不起勁的日子，挑一件有點難、又做得到的小事。
column2: On flat days, pick one small thing that’s a little hard but doable.

column1: =今天有一點點投入的時刻，就值得記下來。
column2: Any moment today when you were absorbed is worth writing down.

column1: =想念的時候，允許自己難過一下，也記得吃飯、睡覺。
column2: When you miss someone, let yourself be sad for a while — and remember to eat and sleep.

column1: =今天不必勉強自己好起來，慢慢來。
column2: You don’t have to force yourself to feel better today. Take your time.

column1: =今天找個時間，放下手機，好好聽一個人說話。
column2: Find a moment today to put your phone down and really listen to someone.

column1: =關係卡住的時候，先照顧好自己，再慢慢靠近。
column2: When a relationship feels stuck, take care of yourself first, then move closer slowly.

column1: =你已經很努力了，對自己溫柔一點，就像對朋友那樣。
column2: You’ve been trying hard. Be gentle with yourself, as you would with a friend.

column1: =把「我不夠好」換成「我正在學」，再試一次。
column2: Swap “I’m not good enough” for “I’m learning”, and try again.

column1: =不知道往哪走時，先做一件這週就能完成的小事。
column2: When you don’t know which way to go, do one small thing you can finish this week.

column1: =方向不必一次想清楚，走一小段，路會慢慢浮現。
column2: You don’t need the whole direction now; walk a little and the path appears.

column1: =三件事都完成了，剩下的時間可以輕鬆一點。
column2: All three things are done — you can take it easy for the rest of the day.

column1: =今天有動起來，身體會謝謝你。
column2: You moved today — your body will thank you.

column1: =運動過的日子，晚上會睡得比較好。
column2: On days you exercise, you tend to sleep better.

column1: =已經專注很久了，起身走一走，讓身體也休息。
column2: You’ve been focused a long time — get up and walk so your body can rest too.

column1: =坐久了，轉轉肩頸、伸伸背，再回來。
column2: You’ve been sitting a while: roll your shoulders, stretch your back, then come back.

column1: =今天還沒動一動，傍晚走個十分鐘也好。
column2: You haven’t moved yet today — even a ten-minute walk this evening helps.

column1: =找個空檔伸展五分鐘，身體鬆了，心也會鬆。
column2: Find five minutes to stretch; when your body loosens, so does your mind.

column1: =今日小語不再是固定公式：依你的狀況，從作息、鼓勵、目標與計畫、運動、進度、靜心的平靜提示、雁書的安心提示裡挑 1–3 句，組合和順序每段時間都不同；驅動力的話只在一天的幾個節點出現，也不一定每天有
column2: Today’s note is no longer a fixed formula: depending on your day, it picks 1–3 lines from routine, encouragement, goals and plans, movement, progress, calm hints (if you meditate) and reassurance (if you write Yanshu letters), in a different mix and order each part of the day; drive lines appear only at certain points of the day, and not every day
Take it slowly — a little progress today is enough.

column1: =做不完的事，留一點給明天也可以。
column2: You can leave some of it for tomorrow.

column1: =回頭看看這週做的事，其實累積了不少。
column2: Look back at this week — you’ve built up more than it seems.
You sat down today; that’s the start.

column1: =辛苦了，今天的你已經很好了。
column2: You’ve worked hard — today you’ve done well.

column1: =想念的時候，先把吃飯、睡覺照顧好。
column2: When you miss someone, take care of eating and sleeping first.

column1: =被誤解時，先等情緒平一點，再想怎麼說。
column2: When you’re misunderstood, let the feeling settle before deciding what to say.

column1: =用對朋友說話的語氣對自己說話，事情會比較好處理。
column2: Talk to yourself the way you’d talk to a friend; things get easier to handle.

column1: =你不是一個人在扛這些，先讓呼吸慢下來。
column2: You’re not carrying this alone. Let your breathing slow down first.

column1: =今天有運動，這是很好的平衡。
column2: You exercised today — a good balance.

column1: =今天有誰因為你而輕鬆一點？
column2: Who had it a little easier today because of you?

column1: =今日小語的語氣更內斂；只有平常書寫比較感性的人，才會看到情感濃一點的說法
column2: Today’s note is more understated; warmer phrasing appears only for people whose own writing is more expressive

column1: =靜心回饋依修行方式回應：行走、慈心、呼吸、身體掃描、開放覺察，先給對應方法的教學和做法（出自《牛的印跡》與智者大師《修習止觀坐禪法要》）
column2: Meditation feedback now follows your method — walking, loving-kindness, breathing, body scan, open awareness — giving that method’s teaching and practical steps first (from Hoofprint of the Ox and Master Zhiyi’s Essentials of Practising Calm and Insight)

column1: =靜心回饋與雁書回信的開頭語氣更內斂；只有平常書寫比較感性、或這次寫得很感性時，才用溫暖一點的說法
column2: Meditation feedback and Yanshu replies open in a more understated tone; warmer phrasing is used only when your writing is usually expressive, or this entry is

column1: =靜心回饋加入帕奧禪師《菩提資糧》〈除妄念經〉的五個方法、阿姜查《森林中的法語》、達賴喇嘛談安忍與平等心；慈心多了平等心與「施與受」的練習
column2: Meditation feedback adds the five methods of the Vitakkasaṇṭhāna Sutta from Pa-Auk Sayadaw’s talks, Ajahn Chah’s forest teachings and the Dalai Lama on patience and equanimity; loving-kindness gains equanimity and “giving and taking” practices

column1: =雁書加入《The Book of Joy》、達賴喇嘛、阿姜查的觀點，並新增「生氣」這類煩惱的回信
column2: Yanshu letters draw on The Book of Joy, the Dalai Lama and Ajahn Chah, and now reply to letters about anger
Relaxing body and mind, silent illumination; plain-spoken
Adjusting body, breath and mind, in clear stages
Watching the mind; easing emotions through reflection
Silent noting; seeing each moment clearly

column1: =經典裡的方法，一步步對治念頭
column2: Methods from the suttas for working with thoughts step by step

column1: =森林禪師，直接看著經驗、放下
column2: Forest master: look directly at experience and let go

column1: =靜心方法選單重新整理：只列有教學可回應的方法，用日常說法：感受呼吸、數呼吸、身體放鬆掃描、慈心祝福、走路靜心、默念標記、看著自己的心、靜靜坐著（開放覺察）；舊的方法名稱照樣對應
column2: The meditation method menu is reorganized: it lists only methods the app has teachings for, in everyday words — feel the breath, count the breath, relaxing body scan, loving-kindness wishes, walking meditation, silent noting, watching the mind itself, just sitting (open awareness). Old method names still map to the same teachings

column1: =靜心回饋加入達賴喇嘛《The Heart of Meditation》與《The Book of Joy》的練習，達賴喇嘛、帕奧禪師現在也能在「指定回應的老師」裡選；老師選單附上每位老師的風格簡介
column2: Meditation feedback adds practices from the Dalai Lama's The Heart of Meditation and The Book of Joy; the Dalai Lama and Pa-Auk Sayadaw can now be chosen as the responding teacher, and the teacher menu shows a short note on each teacher's style

column1: =靜心回饋語料擴充：聲音、悲傷、身體緊繃、坐不住、懷疑、批判自己等狀況多了不同老師的說法，同一種問題每次的回答更多元
column2: Meditation feedback has more material: sounds, sadness, tension, restlessness, doubt and self-judgment now draw on more teachers, so the same kind of problem gets more varied answers
e.g. Buddha recitation, mindful yoga, mantra

column1: =每一題，點出你可能會這樣做的選項，可以複選（最多 3 個）；都不像就選「都不太像我」。不用比較哪個最像、哪個最不像，照直覺點就好。
column2: For each question, tap the options you might actually do — you can pick up to 3. If none fit, choose "None of these is really me". No need to decide which is most or least like you; just go with your gut.
None of these is really me

column1: =「我的最佳狀態」的生活情境題改成複選：點出你可能會這樣做的選項（最多 3 個），也可以選「都不太像我」，不用再勉強挑最像和最不像
column2: The life-situation questions in "My Best State" are now multi-select: tap the options you might do (up to 3), or choose "None of these is really me" — no more forcing a most-like and least-like pick
